description: I’m a biomedical engineer and Senior Engineer interested in medical technology, software, innovation, and space exploration. I enjoy solving technical problems and turning ideas into practical solutions. For this project, I want to build a system that helps monitor and support people in space. I’m looking for teammates with skills in software, AI, data, UI/UX, aerospace, biomedical engineering, sensors, and teamwork.
summary:
AeroNYX is an innovative astronaut health monitoring platform designed to support physical and psychological well-being during long-duration space missions. Astronauts face significant health risks from space radiation, altered gravity, isolation, and confined environments, potentially leading to bone loss, cardiovascular changes, nutritional deficiencies, and mental health challenges.
AeroNYX enables daily health assessments by analyzing blood and urine samples to monitor indicators of bone loss, vitamin deficiencies, and glucose levels. It also tracks vital signs, including heart rate and body temperature, to identify early signs of health deterioration. Based on these findings, the platform provides health alerts and recommendations using available onboard medical resources.
The platform includes ASTRO, a chatbot designed to support behavioral health, stress management, and emotional well-being. AeroNYX also monitors environmental conditions, including radiation exposure, air pressure, and temperature.
Health reports can be transmitted to flight surgeons on Earth, enabling medical teams to assess health trends, guide treatment decisions, and prepare preventive care plans. AeroNYX aims to improve astronaut safety through proactive, personalized healthcare during space exploration.
details:
What is it? AeroNYX is a physical and mental health monitoring device for astronauts on long missions. It monitors blood and urine specimens, tracks radiation dose, dispenses medications, and tracks the onboard med kit. Every astronaut will also be able to see their total radiation dose accumulated throughout their career and will warn when approaching limit or exceeded. Alongside the radiation dose, live space weather reports are provided through NASA’s DONKI service. The built-in companion, Astro, provides a mental health check-in to help astronauts through isolation-related and other mental health issues that arise in space. Astro will monitor sleep and stress, run check-ins every login, and offer calming activities to aid. Test results are compared to pre-flight baselines as well as the continuously stored readings throughout the mission and are communicated to the flight surgeon, along with messaging between the flight surgeon directly through the platform. 

Benefits and Impact: On a deep-space mission it is vital for an astronaut to maintain good health. AeroNYX puts physical health, medication, radiation exposure, and mental health in one place the astronaut can access instantly, and gives the flight surgeon one clear report. Checking in on stress becomes a normal daily step

What is creative. Currently, individual devices, resources, or people are needed to cover body, medication, space environment and mind; our device integrates all components into one platform. Every reading is compared with the astronaut’s own baseline, not only a general range. The mental health check-in meant to be personable and comforting, not just a form. 

Tools: The platform was built using HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no framework and no build step. Web Crypto API was used for the lock and encryption. Astro’s voice is from ElevenLabs. NASA’s DONKI API provides space weather data. 75 automated tests were performed on Node.js. Git, GitHub and GitHub Pages. Python, Playwright and ffmpeg for the demo video. We used Claude, an AI assistant, for coding help and for the device drawings, which are marked on screen and listed in AI-USE.md in the repository. No hardware was built.

What we considered. Privacy: the health record will be encrypted on the tablet with badge and password/pin protection to protect Protected Health Information (PHI). For the demo, we disabled that layer for easier access to the dashboard. All the data is simulated, not real data. Safety: AeroNYX never diagnoses or prescribes; the flight surgeon decides, and Astro hands off to the astronauts. Honesty: simulated data and AI-made drawings are labelled. Crew time: few words, clear graphics, answers by tapping. We used NASA’s thresholds, not our own.
